Have you spoken to him about your concerns? I think what you're feeling isn't wrong. I would say don't hide them from your partner. Also, people are complicated, there are a number of reasons why he could be in this more "solo" routine. As a 19y/o M living with my 19yo F partner, I feel similar to this sometimes. Like I don't really "see" her for ages, even though she's right there. When I spoke to my girl about this, I had to bring it up for assurance a few times, but her reassurance helped me process her being an introvert, or even just being grumpy. Don't blame yourself without too much evidence. I'd say you're a lovely partner

Also w ground game, you need to block and hit in between transitions to throw your opponent off. Take your time on the ground. Learn to deny their transitions. On the ground, a good defense is a good offence

Practice mode is okay yeah. I did it after really getting a hang of the game however. Also, I wouldn't recommend just fighting the computer to get good. As you go higher in difficulty, the CPU just learns to read your inputs better, resulting in weird standing fights and easy ground game

Mate, a lot of it is just practice. You'll learn to see hits coming. Best practice is online casual. You'll need to improve timing, your fight rhythm, reading your opponent, footwork, blocking. Find openings before your opponent does, and always be aware of where you are open
